title: The verified rung is unreachable: nothing supplies verifiedTicketIds
body:
`TriageInput.verifiedTicketIds` is documented as the channel by which a crawler finding or
a maintainer's repro promotes a ticket straight to `verified` — the highest promotion
state — and it is consumed in `triagePlaytestCorpus` (src/qa/triage.ts:197).

Nothing supplies it. Not `bin/triage.ts`, not `loop.sh`, not any script; a repo-wide
search finds only the declaration and the read. So `verified` is unreachable by
construction. The live dev-loop exercise hit the symptom without the cause: "I had no
reproduction to pass as verifiedTicketIds."

Separately, `rank.ts` calls crawler+fleet agreement "the strongest signal"
(BOTH_SOURCES_BONUS = 2), but `sessionIssueRecords` stamps every issue `source: "fleet"`
(src/qa/triage.ts:94) and triage reads only the playtest corpus, so no QA ticket can
contain a crawler finding and that bonus is dead on the path feeding the dev loop.

CORRECTION TO AN EARLIER VERSION OF THIS SUBMISSION

A previous filing claimed this would give a single-vendor operator a route to
corroboration, and that the hard part was identity matching. Both were wrong, and the
second was wrong in the useful direction:

  - The converter already exists. `crawlerIssueRecords` in src/feedback/compile.ts turns
    findings into IssueRecords with `source: "crawler"` and `text = "<CODE>: <message>"`.
    It is private to that module, so the wiring is an export plus an optional input on
    TriageInput — smaller than estimated, not larger.

  - But incidental agreement would fire RARELY, so this is not a general corroboration
    route. The crawler's codes are CRASH, INTEGRITY, DESYNC, PERSIST, LEGALITY, SOFTLOCK,
    RENDER, WORLD — invariant violations. Playtesters overwhelmingly report comprehension
    and copy defects: contradictory oath text, a mechanical consequence hidden from a
    summary, prose naming a verb the action surface rejects. Those are different CLASSES
    of defect, not different wordings of one, so a crawler finding and a player complaint
    will seldom be about the same thing at all.

    The wording gap compounds it. Crawler text is terse and machine-shaped; the merge
    threshold is calibrated at 0.15 against human-authored prose, and "SOFTLOCK: no legal
    action from steading_yard" shares very little token mass with "the blocked exit says
    both approach routes are selected when exactly one was."

WHAT THAT IMPLIES

The `verified` rung is the part actually worth building, and it is a different mechanism
from clustering: a DELIBERATE reproduction of a named ticket, not incidental overlap. It
should be a targeted check — take an actionable ticket's location and claim, try to
reproduce it deterministically, and pass the id if it reproduces — rather than hoping the
two instruments happen to describe one defect in similar words.

Making BOTH_SOURCES_BONUS live by feeding crawler findings into triage is cheap and worth
doing on its own merits (it puts real invariant violations in front of the dev loop, which
today they never reach), but it should be justified as coverage rather than as
corroboration, and nobody should expect it to unblock a single-vendor operator.

Worth measuring before either: how often, across the existing corpus, a crawler finding
and a playtest finding actually land on the same canonical location. If that number is
near zero, only the deliberate-repro route is worth the code.

evidence.summary: verifiedTicketIds is never supplied and crawler findings never enter triage; a deliberate repro is the route worth building, not incidental clustering.
